entries.title: Saddle up
notes: Mounts have arrived. The first is the Bay Horse: a bay with a black mane and tail, a white blaze, a red saddle blanket trimmed in gold, a leather saddle, stirrups and a bridle.
Press V (rebindable in Controls) to call your mount and climb into the saddle, and press it again to get down. Your hero sits astride with feet in the stirrups.
The horse walks, trots and gallops as you go faster, rocking into a gallop and kicking up dust. When it stands still it breathes, swishes its tail and now and then lowers its head.
Riding is faster than running: a canter when walking and a full gallop when running.
Attacking, casting or taking damage puts you back on your feet. You cannot ride in dungeons or into lava.
Mounts are not dropped anywhere yet.

entries.title: The archer, in light
notes: Every archer shot has new 3D effects. Arrows fly as arrows of light with fletching and a streak of wind behind them: gold for a plain shot and the skill's colour for a skill. Each one strikes with a spark and a flash, and the bow flares as it looses.
Piercing Arrow tears a blazing gold line through everything in its path.
Rain of Arrows marks the ground with a golden sigil, arrows of light fall onto it out of the sky, and the ground is left bristling with arrows.
Frost Arrow bursts ice crystals out of the ground. Poison Arrow splashes into a toxic green cloud. Explosive Arrow blows up in fire and scorches the ground.
Explosive Trap sits armed on a turning fire sigil before it blows, cracking the earth.
Starfall Arrow calls a falling star down in a pillar of light.
Eagle Eye wreathes the archer in gold, and Evasive Roll leaves a streak of wind.
Archer subclass skills now use the new 3D effects too: strikes fire a shot of light into the target, and the area, nova, buff and dash skills look like the knight's.
The archer effects need Enhanced rendering and Enhanced effects in Graphics, like the knight's and the mage's. The archer's armour and body were already remastered with the other classes.

entries.title: Proper great helms
notes: Knight helmets are no longer pointed. They are great helms with a round dome, a flat faceplate with a ridge down the middle, a brow over the eye slit, a long faceplate coming down to the chin and a flared guard over the neck.
An archer's metal helmets take the same great-helm shape. Mage and archer hoods are soft and round over the head instead of peaked.

entries.title: Heroes remastered
notes: Every hero body and every piece of armour has been remastered with real materials. Steel is polished and mirrors the sky, gold shines and is engraved, dark iron has a dull sheen, chain mail and dragon scale catch the light, leather has grain, cloth has a soft woven sheen, and gems sparkle.
Heroes are smoothly shaded now instead of faceted, while plate edges stay crisp.

Helmets have been reshaped. A knight's helm is taller and squarer with a ridge along the crown, a pointed faceplate, a longer jaw down to the chin and a guard over the back of the neck. Mage and archer hoods rise into a peak that falls back over the head, with a face opening as long as a face.
Heroes' faces have a longer jaw and chin, so heads look like heads rather than balls.
A mage's robes and hoods are always cloth and an archer's jerkins and hoods are always leather, whatever their colour.
Monsters no longer have a glow, glowing veins, a coloured aura or a pool of light under them. Bosses keep their rune ring.
Fixed armour sometimes going invisible after the game unloaded unused assets.
The new hero materials need Enhanced rendering in Graphics.

entries.title: Arcane fire, real shadows and weapons put away
notes: Every mage spell has new 3D effects. Bolts, fireballs, ice shards and arcane missiles fly as glowing shots with trails: fire sheds embers and smoke, ice is a spinning crystal, arcane missiles wrap a turning rune, and each bursts in a flare that lights up the ground.
Fireball blooms into a fiery blast that leaves burning cracks. Ice Shard and Frost Nova burst ice crystals out of the ground. Chain Lightning forks and re-strikes between its targets.

Meteor falls burning out of the sky onto a fiery sigil and cracks the earth. Blizzard rains ice over a frost sigil. Arcane Cataclysm gathers over a turning violet sigil and erupts in a pillar of light.
Rejuvenate spirals green light up round you, Arcane Barrier raises a blue hex ward, and Blink leaves a streak of violet light behind you.
Heroes, townsfolk and monsters now cast solid shadows on the ground instead of faint slivers.
Out of combat your hero puts their weapon away: a sword and shield go on the back, a staff or bow across it. They come back to hand the moment you fight or cast.
More gaps in the town walls are closed, including where the walls meet the gate towers of Lorenmar and Valcrest.
The mage effects need Enhanced rendering and Enhanced effects in Graphics, like the knight's.

entries.title: The knight, reforged in light
notes: Every knight attack has new 3D effects: each swing of the three-hit combo leaves a sweeping sword trail with a white-hot edge in your weapon's colour, the overhead chop cracks the ground with a shockwave, and every blow lands with a star flare and sparks.
Power Strike carves a great golden crescent and bursts on impact. Cleave sweeps a huge arc trailing wind. Shield Bash throws a glowing ward forward.
Ground Slam and Leap Strike tear glowing cracks in the earth, send out a shockwave and dust wall, and throw rock shards. Leap Strike also leaves a light trail and a golden sigil where you land.
Judgement draws a turning holy sigil, then a great sword of light falls from the sky and a pillar of light erupts where it strikes.

Whirlwind spins blade trails and wind round you. Battle Roar and War Cry wreathe you in flame with sound waves rolling out. Second Wind spirals green light up round you. Iron Skin raises a golden hex ward.
Path skills for knights (strikes, novas, slams, hammers, buffs and dashes) use the new effects too. Big hits briefly light up the ground around them.
Quick attacks no longer pile their trails into a ball of light: each new swing fades the last.
These need Enhanced rendering and Enhanced effects in Graphics; with them off you get the original effects.
Chat fixed: what you type no longer runs over the 'Press Enter to chat' hint, the hint hides while you type, and typed text matches the box.
Chat text now grows with the Text size setting while staying inside the chat box, the newest message always stays in view, and turning off Show chat now hides the whole chat.

entries.title: Back on your feet after dying
notes: After you fall and rise again in town, your hero stands up and moves normally instead of staying stuck in the death pose.
The same fix applies when you rise at a raid checkpoint.

entries.title: Living forests, real shadows and new effects
notes: Town and castle walls are joined up: the gaps where wall sections met towers, gates and corners are closed.

Every tree and bush has been rebuilt with full leafy crowns made of thousands of real leaves: broadleaf, pine needles, hanging willow and blossom. Leaves sway in the wind, catch the light at their edges, and each tree has its own slightly different colour.
Realtime shadows: torches, braziers and campfires now cast soft shadows of the people, walls and trees around them, and sun shadows near you are sharper.

Enhanced effects: spells, hits, explosions and impacts throw 3D sparks, glowing embers, smoke, dust and flying shards, and big blasts briefly light up the ground and buildings around them. Fires give off drifting embers and smoke.
New Enhanced effects option in Graphics. It is on by default and off on the Low preset, and needs Enhanced rendering.

entries.title: Mist over the Shadowfen
notes: The Shadowfen is wrapped in distance fog: a grey-green mist that stays thin around you and closes into a wall further off, drifting in slow banks and lying low over the water and reeds so the trees rise out of it.
The mist turns a cold blue-grey by night and fades in and out as you cross the swamp's border.
It follows the Atmosphere setting in Graphics.

entries.title: Minimap and region banner fixed
notes: The compass round the minimap is drawn whole: its N, E, S and W markers and points are no longer cut off.
The region banner under the minimap grows to fit the name, so long names like The Bloodmoor keep both pointed ends.
The gold claws round the health and mana orbs are drawn whole, with their gems.

entries.title: Orb frames fixed
notes: The health and mana orbs are no longer cut off at the bottom: their gold rings and claw mounts are drawn whole.

entries.title: Rebuilt structures
notes: Caves are rebuilt: a craggy, layered rock outcrop with a real tunnel running back into the dark, a rocky lip around the mouth, timber props and a lintel, torches on iron brackets, rock teeth over the entrance, rubble at the foot and a faint firelight deep inside.

Monster camps are rebuilt: hide tents stretched over A-frame poles and a ridge pole, sagging between them, with sewn seams and patches, door flaps tied back on a dark inside, guy ropes pegged to stakes and a fur at the door.
Campfires are a ring of fire-blackened stones around glowing embers, with logs leaning together and real tongues of flame.
Lair pillars are rough-hewn stone blocks stacked on a stepped plinth under a capstone, chipped and worn, carved with glowing runes, with rubble at the foot and a living flame in the fire bowls.

Boulders, stone circles, ruins, graves, wells and the dungeons' columns, pillars, obelisks and stalagmites are sculpted: craggy rock, chipped and broken masonry, ruined columns with jagged broken tops.
Houses and halls get ridge tiles along their roofs, stone sills under the lit windows and timber lintels over them.

entries.title: Menacing monsters
notes: Every monster is reworked: a darker, harsher hide with glowing veins crawling slowly over it, lit from below by a pool of its land's colour and edged with a burning aura.

Each land has its own colour: sickly green in the fields and the fen, frost blue on the peaks, ember orange in the waste, violet in the void and Gloomwood, blood red on the Bloodmoor. Higher-tier monsters glow stronger.
Monsters flare up when they fight you, and their ground glow brightens.
Bosses stand on a slowly turning ring of jagged runes, with embers rising off them and a light of their colour on them at night.
New Graphics option: Menacing monsters (on for Medium and up).

entries.title: Clear water and mystical townsfolk
notes: Water is rebuilt: you see the lake bed through the surface, bent by the waves, fading into deep blue as it gets deeper, with the sky and sun reflected on top, light dancing on the shallows and foam breaking along the shore.

The people of Aldara shine: quest givers stand on slowly turning golden sigils with motes of light rising around them and a warm glow at night, priests in holy blue, merchants, innkeepers and smiths with an amber light.
Every townsperson gets richer cloth, gilded trim that catches the light, grounded feet and a soft aura at the edges.
New Graphics option: Mystical townsfolk (on for Medium and up).

entries.title: Realm of Aldara, rebuilt
notes: The Unity edition is now the game. Press Play in the launcher and Realm of Aldara starts in its new engine, with the characters you already have.
High-resolution ground: grass, dirt paths, rock faces, sand, snow, ash and swamp mud now have sharp, detailed surfaces that catch the light, instead of the soft painted map.
Depth of field is now off by default and no longer part of any quality preset, so the world stays sharp. Turn it on in Settings, Graphics, if you want it.
New Graphics option: High-resolution ground (on for Medium and up).
If the launcher asks you to, close it and open it again once so it can finish updating itself.

entries.title: Realm of Aldara Classic is here
notes: Realm of Aldara Classic, the whole game rebuilt in Unity, can now be installed from the launcher. Find it at the top of the Home page and press Install.
Classic picks up the characters you already have, so you can carry on where you left off. The browser edition stays as it is and still opens with Play.

Classic adds enhanced rendering: ambient occlusion, soft shadows, a moving sun and moon, torchlight on models at night, deeper water, molten lava, rocky cliffs and wind-blown grass. Turn any of it off in Settings, Graphics.
New Graphics settings: aspect ratio, resolution and a working world zoom. The interface now scales to fit any screen shape, and Interface has a Whole interface size.
The launcher keeps Classic up to date, downloading only the files that change, and updates itself to do so. If Classic does not appear yet, close the launcher and open it again.

entries.title: Smooth sliding along mountains
notes: Running into a mountainside, a cliff, the coast or a building at an angle now slides you smoothly along it instead of catching on its edge or stopping dead.
Hitting a wall nearly head-on still lets you glide along it at a little over half speed, so you can steer around mountains without fighting them.
In a tight pocket between two walls you now stand still instead of shaking back and forth.

entries.title: New HUD layout
notes: The bottom of the screen now holds only what you use in a fight: your health and mana orbs, the skill bar, vials and auto-combat.
Character, Inventory, Skills, Quests, Map, Dungeons, Vault, Guild, Play Together and Settings have moved to their own menu in the bottom-right corner, grouped by type, like a classic MMO.
On smaller windows the menu stands up along the right edge instead.
Settings now has a gear icon.

entries.title: Smoother frame rate, sun shafts and camera zoom
notes: Dynamic resolution: when frames run long the game trims the render resolution first (every effect stays on) and gives it back once things are smooth.
Render resolution Auto now follows your quality preset, up to 4K on Ultra. The FPS counter shows the current resolution.
Lights are drawn from cached glow sprites, which saves time every frame.
The game drops to 30 frames a second while another window has focus, to save power and heat (can be turned off in Settings).
Sun shafts and depth haze on High and Ultra.
The screen edges pulse red when your health is below 30%.
Camera zoom with the mouse wheel or the + and - keys, middle-click resets it.
F8 hides the interface for a clean view.
Backpack items show how their stats compare to what you are wearing.
New option: Sound in the background.

entries.title: Sharper graphics
notes: The world now draws at your screen's full resolution. Before, zooming in drew a smaller picture and stretched it, which made everything blurry.
Characters, monsters, bosses, pets, text and effects stay crisp at every World zoom level, and on high-density displays.
New Render resolution setting on the Graphics page: Auto (sharp, eases off on very large screens), Full, High, Medium, or Low (the old look). Lower it if the game runs slowly.

entries.title: Music, display modes and a new raid title
notes: Music: every town, zone and dungeon has its own tracks, crossfading as you travel between them. Quiet places leave a little silence between songs.
Boss music: an intro plays when a boss comes into view, its battle theme fades in when the fight starts, and it fades out when the boss falls (or you do).
A Music volume slider is on the Sound page.
Settings: Sound is now a page inside Settings, and the graphics card options are on the Graphics page.
Display mode setting on the Graphics page: Windowed, Borderless windowed or Fullscreen. The desktop game remembers your choice.
New glowing title, Breaker of the Eclipse, for completing the Vault of the Eclipse raid.
Fixed skill cooldown numbers getting stuck at 1 on the skill bar.
Jewelry can now be dismantled, and Auto Dismantle includes weaker jewelry.
Knights now hear their swing and grunt when attacking thin air.
The Celestial Phoenix pet is back to its original model.
Launcher: the update source option is gone. The launcher now updates itself, and downloads the music with the game.

entries.title: Glowing titles really glow
notes: Glowing titles (Legend of Aldara, The Ascended, Voidwalker, Dungeon Conqueror, Godforged, The Relentless) now shine over your head: a halo of light that breathes, a band of light that sweeps across the letters, and small twinkles.
The same glow shows on the title under your portrait and in the titles list in your Inventory.

entries.title: New bosses, new sounds, and the game gets its own program
notes: All sixteen bosses have new models: Goblin Warchief, Bone Tyrant, Shadowfen Dragon, Frost Giant King, Infernal Lord, Void Emperor, Grak the Goblin King, Lich Morvain, Queen Glacia, Ignar the Forgemaster, The Hollow King, Nerissa the Tide Queen, Arachna, Countess Sanguine, The Grand Artificer and Astraeus.
Every boss has its own animations: idle, walk, a flinch when hit, a death, and a matching animation for each of its attacks, timed to the wind-up and the strike.
Nerissa, Arachna, Countess Sanguine, The Grand Artificer and Astraeus now fight with their own signature moves instead of generic ones.
Sound is in: 505 recorded sounds for weapon swings, two-layer hits, blocks, parries, crits, seven spell schools and enemy spells.
Your character has a voice: grunts on attacks, casts, pain, death, and heavy breathing at low health. Choose Human male, Human female, Orc or Off in Settings, Sound.
Creatures growl when they notice you, attack, get hurt and die: wolves and beasts, trolls and giants, ghouls and undead, spiders, wraiths and human enemies.
The launcher and the game are now separate. The launcher installs the game, keeps it updated, and pressing Play closes the launcher and opens the game in its own window.
If you have the old launcher, download the new one once from the link. From then on the launcher installs and updates everything.

entries.title: The Aldara Launcher
notes: The game now opens on a launcher with a Home page, this Updates and Hotfixes page and Settings.
New versions download by themselves when the launcher opens. No more re-downloading the game.
Your saves stay on your computer and are never touched by an update.
Settings: automatic updates, check for updates, graphics card choice and a button to open your saves folder.
If the update server cannot be reached, you can still play the version you have.

entries.title: Raid enemy names
notes: Every enemy in the Vault of the Eclipse has a new name: Gloam Wretches, Duskguard Spearmen, Shade Chanters, Emberhelm Templars, Glyphbound Sentinels, Heralds of Dusk and Dawn, Veilrenders, the Sealwarden Behemoth and the Spanwatch Revenant.
The twin bosses are now the Twin Regents, Vesper and Solace.
The final boss is now Maelthar, the Sunless King, and the Templars drop Sun Embers.

entries.title: Raids: the Vault of the Eclipse
notes: A new Raids tab in the Dungeons window, for up to 4 players. Requires level 100.

Eight sections and six encounters: the plates of the Eclipsed Gate, the Shattered Descent, the Hall of the Oracles glyph puzzle, the levers of the Sunken Gallery, the Twin Regents, the Eclipse Bridge hold-out and Maelthar, the Sunless King.
Waves of enemies during every encounter, enrage timers and wipe mechanics.
Checkpoints are saved: leave and continue later, and a wipe sends the whole party back to the last one.
Fallen players can be revived by an ally standing over them.
A hidden cache on the way, and a treasury full of loot at the end.

entries.title: Knight skill animations
notes: New one-handed and two-handed animations for all 11 knight skills.
Every Paladin, Berserker, Guardian and Blademaster ability has its own animation.
New hit reactions and a new death animation for the knight.
Bladestorm spins for its whole duration and Undying Rage plays when it saves you.

entries.title: New pet models, walk and run
notes: All 19 pets have brand new models, with walking, flying, idle and attack motion.
Press Ctrl to switch between walking and running. You walk by default.
A Walking or Running tag sits in the bottom left corner; click it to switch.

entries.title: Warrior animations
notes: New combat idle, walk, run and three-hit combo for the knight with sword and shield.
New two-handed set for greatswords, including a new whirlwind.
The shield now turns to face your enemies.

entries.title: Mythic armor models
notes: Every mythic armor set has a new model, with its glowing aura.

entries.title: Subclass window fix
notes: Fixed the subclass window crashing for characters with a broken saved subclass. Their points are refunded and the next choice is free.
The combat sound pack is switched off for now.

entries.label: Earlier
entries.title: Armor, weapons and quality of life
notes: New armor models for every class and tier, with helmets that hide your hair and closed faceplates.
New weapon models for swords, staves and bows.
Auto combat uses your subclass abilities.
Level scaling: being far above a monster's level now makes a real difference.
Inventory tabs and sorting.
